iconicAnchor.label: Royal Automobile Club rooms designed for sustained social ritual
iconicAnchor.creatorOrTradition: Edwardian club architecture and private social interiors
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Historic England's documented clubhouse interior anchors the style in purpose-built rooms for conversation, reading, dining, and recurring member use rather than generic dark luxury.

sources.title: The interior of the club room at the Pall Mall clubhouse of the Royal Automobile Club
supports: A purpose-built club room combines formal enclosure, furniture groupings, and a setting for recurring member activity.
The historic interior supports the guide's emphasis on collected material, quiet order, and social use.

sources.title: Lansdowne House, Westminster
supports: The Lansdowne Club combined dining, restaurant, bar, athletic, and residential spaces within one layered house identity.
Its architectural history supports treating private-club design as an organized social environment, not a single lounge image.
